problems.stem: A readiness checklist has four boxes (syllabus posted, modules visible, gradebook set up, links work), all checked. What is the strongest critique?
options: The course is ready; all four boxes are checked.
Those are setup facts; readiness means a student can complete the capstone with the scaffolds they were given.
Add a fifth box for the course banner image.
Readiness only requires that the links work.
problems.explanation: A working link is a setup fact, not evidence that the student's path through the capstone is supported.

problems.stem: The capstone evidence board has a 'limitations' panel, but no earlier activity ever asked students to state a limitation. What does a path-level review do?
options: Nothing; students can figure out limitations at the capstone.
Add a prior activity, such as a Module 6 reflection that asks for one named limitation, so the panel is scaffolded.
Remove the limitations panel from the capstone.
Move the capstone earlier in the term.
problems.explanation: Each capstone panel needs a prior building activity; front-loading all demands at the capstone overloads learners.

problems.stem: An instructor uses AI to generate a readiness checklist. What is the strongest boundary?
options: Adopt the AI checklist unchanged because it is thorough.
Use the AI checklist, then trace each capstone panel back to a building activity yourself before going live.
Skip the checklist and trust the course looks done.
Ask AI only to format the checklist nicely.
problems.explanation: AI can list items, but the instructor must verify path-level readiness against the actual course.

problems.stem: The AI-use policy is in the syllabus but the disclosure-requiring assignment never links to it. Why does this fail readiness?
options: It does not fail; the policy exists somewhere in the course.
Students will not connect the requirement to the rule unless the policy is referenced at the point of use.
The policy should simply be deleted from the syllabus.
Readiness is about links working, not policy placement.
problems.explanation: A policy present but not referenced where it applies is unlikely to shape student behavior.
